features.scope_note: The two inflected tenses do not map one-to-one to modern English simple/progressive/perfect categories; prior present-for-future remains in force.

features.description: A simple preterite can express action earlier than another past viewpoint.
features.scope_note: Relative anteriority can be made explicit in translation without inventing an Old English compound form.

features.description: Finite habban with a selected transitive past participle expresses a completed action or present/past result.
features.scope_note: The auxiliary agrees with the subject, while the accusative object is the patient of the participle. Selected bare participles are productive. Object-agreeing alternatives are recognized/accepted only within independently supported inflection; no arbitrary causative or intransitive have-perfect is introduced.

features.description: Recognize wesan with an intransitive past participle, specifically gewiten.
features.scope_note: The subject is the departing participant; the phrase is not passive merely because it contains be. Recognize the contextual completed-departure meaning; no unrestricted productive system.

features.description: Recognize wesan with a present participle, specifically sittende.
features.scope_note: Context may motivate simple, progressive or durative English. A simple finite Old English verb may also receive progressive English. No obligatory modern progressive category is inferred.

features.description: Compare an active transitive clause with a supported agentless passive and distinguish event from resulting state.
features.scope_note: Retains prior u07-passive: a passive subject is the affected entity; converting to agentless passive omits any named active agent. Wearð may focus on coming into the condition, wæs on a state or contextually an event. No mechanical became/was rule or fram-agent production.

features.description: Express simultaneous, anterior and intended-later time relative to a reporting viewpoint.
features.scope_note: Prior report subjunctives provide simultaneous sīe/wǣre; anterior hæfde plus selected participle is new. Hæfde is syncretic and context identifies the report function. Wolde plus infinitive retains volition/intention and does not guarantee later realization. Indicative reports may be defensible; no automatic backshift or subjunctive=false.

features.description: Intransitive cease/fail without an expressed genitive object, including seedtime and harvest ceasing or failing in Cook19.16. Earlier genitive cessation remains available for ceasing from rule.
Accusative person killed; distinguishes this lethal sense from previously taught strike/smite.
Seeing is asserted absolutely in the bounded temporal clauses of Cook20.2; no accusative object must be invented.
On+dative with rich/lowly predicates; not physical motion into the noun.
Beforan+dative marks the person before whom someone is sent; extends earlier static location explicitly.
Accusative thing prepared; with the selected past participle, habban retains that accusative patient.
Accusative text or letter written; prior morphology does not itself establish this lexical frame.
Accusative person/thing sent and dative recipient; beforan+dative is a separate ahead-of frame.
Accusative thing thrown, including the assigned hook.
Welig on+dative identifies the thing or resource in which a person, place or productive event is rich; includes harvest rich in fruit.
Ābūtan+accusative, surrounding a person/thing or building around it.
Selected accusative after sending among a group; the directly attested sheep/wolves passage supports this precise use. Dative location is also attested but is not the selected productive frame.
Æt+dative marks the person from whom one learns, as in leornian æt a person.
For+dative identifies the beneficiary in the assigned payment/giving expression; not every for-case or causal use.
Accusative quantity of time expresses duration.
features.scope_note: The supplied forty-years phrase is explicitly local support; this does not establish all numeral systems.

features.description: A numeral plus genitive measure noun can state breadth or height.
features.scope_note: The measure noun fōt is separately taught in full; the twenty-feet quantity remains supplied local support.

features.description: Nǣfre and preverbal ne reinforce one negative meaning.
features.scope_note: Bounded never/never again constructions only; nǣfre mā means never more/again. Do not teach a general negative-pronoun family by implication.

features.description: Predicative genitive identifies a possessor; predicative possessive adjectives agree with what is possessed.
features.scope_note: Distinguish an owner in genitive from ðīn in the gender/number of dæg or niht. Earlier attributive forms are reused with an explicit new syntax milestone.

features.description: Quantitative predicative mā means more in number with a plural subject.
features.scope_note: Selected indeclinable mā plus prior ðonne comparison standard; distinct from earlier adverbial amount of doing. No new māran comparative-adjective system is required.

features.description: On+accusative with adjectival ōðer may have an understood city noun.
features.scope_note: Supplied local on ōðre [ceastre] analysis, using the actual prior ceaster system; no unrestricted nominal ellipsis production is inferred.

features.description: Two separated swā tokens express equality of degree.
features.scope_note: First swā is degree; second swā introduces the standard. Bind each to the actual prior swa-invariant form and its new sense; do not invent a compound form spanning the intervening adjective.

features.description: Swā plus a nominal compares the persons sent to sheep.
features.scope_note: Explicit bounded extension beyond the prior finite comparative clause.

features.description: Recognize the selected past reported condition and possibility in the Picts and Scots passage.
features.scope_note: Source-specific gif ... gefultumoden and ðæt ... meahten are supplied/analyzed in context. This does not promote a complete new conditional or modal subjunctive system.

features.description: Finding accusative rest may include the dative beneficiaries.
features.scope_note: Declared application of Cook160–161 general dative-of-benefit syntax to the bounded Cook21.9 requirement; not a separately quoted dictionary valency witness. It does not require a preposition translating English unto.

features.description: Supplied nāh for the negative possession clause in Cook20.4.
features.scope_note: Reuse already supplied nis for the other local negative clause; full negative systems are not production.
